subject: Status bulletin — intermittent generation pauses during short high-throughput bursts
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightleaf.ai>, BrightLeaf Support <support@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Status bulletin — intermittent generation pauses during short high-throughput bursts

Hi Elena / BrightLeaf team,

Short note to let you know we’re investigating a pattern of short generation pauses that affected a subset of high-throughput burst requests to the hosted inference API this morning (US region). We surfaced the issue on our status page: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/2028-07-29-high-throughput-pauses.

Impact summary:
- Window: ~15:36–15:54 UTC (approx).
- Symptom: 1–3 second pauses mid-generation followed by normal completion for ~0.4% of requests matching your traffic profile (short bursts of many concurrent small prompts).
- Scope: Affected a small number of hosted API customers using the default routing policy; BrightLeaf saw elevated retry rates for batch writeback jobs.

Immediate mitigation in place:
- We enabled a routing fallback to a model-variant with a different KV/cache eviction profile to reduce mid-run stalls.
- Autoscaling pool increased headroom in the US-west cluster for burst traffic.

What we’re doing next:
- SRE and Runtime teams are doing a detailed timeline and collecting KV cache metrics.
- We’ll share a lightweight timeline and a follow-up within 48 hours.

If you have logs or Kibana links showing the exact request IDs, please forward them — that will speed triage. We’ve attached a CSV timeline extracted from our telemetry for early visibility.

Apologies for the disruption — we take these seriously and will follow up with root cause and long-term mitigations.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Aug 2028 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: incident summary and postmortem (US high-throughput pauses, 2028-07-29)

Elena / BrightLeaf team — Thanks again for the quick collaboration and for sharing request IDs and traces. Below is a concise post-incident summary and next steps. We’ve also published a formal postmortem and remediation plan: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4721 (read-only).

Summary:
- Root cause: A contention window in our KV cache eviction path when handling many concurrent small requests triggered a short-lived stall in token generation for ~0.4% of matching bursts. The contention was exposed by a combination of a recently adjusted eviction tuning parameter and a higher-than-usual burst profile from several customers.
- Impact: Brief mid-generation pauses (1–3s) for a subset of requests in US-west; no truncated generations or lost outputs observed. BrightLeaf observed retries and slightly elevated ingestion latency.
- Detection & mitigation: SRE triggered a routing fallback to a model-variant with an isolated KV cache behavior and temporarily increased pool headroom. These mitigations removed the observed pauses within ~20 minutes of detection.

Remediations completed:
- Reverted the aggressive eviction tweak and deployed a graduated backoff for lock acquisition in the cache eviction path.
- Added a per-customer burst-profile throttle option to avoid exposing other customers to cross-traffic eviction pressure.
- Improved telemetry: we added a KV-eviction spike alert and a new tracing annotation for model-variant fallbacks.

Customer impact and compensation:
- We recognize the disruption to BrightLeaf’s ingestion pipeline. As a gesture, we’re issuing a one-time service credit equivalent to 5% of July usage for your account (applied to the next billing invoice).

What we’ll do differently going forward:
- Run a targeted load test simulating short, high-concurrency bursts against the KV path and include this in the pre-merge CI performance gate.
- Documented the incident and will publish a short technical blog explaining the eviction behavior and how the model-variant fallback avoids stalls.

Attachments: redwood-postmortem-20280806.pdf (summary + timeline)

If you’d like a short 20-minute run-through of the postmortem with your engineers, I can schedule it — otherwise we’ll consider this incident closed after you confirm no residual issues.

Thanks for your patience and partnership,
Jordan Blake
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
